view.text: The lane becomes an alley. A man stands in a lit doorway and will not look at you. Under the porch across from him a tide board runs with chalk.
view.holding: The rain is not a room. He said so.

location.asset: The board is a wash of chalk. Pegs for the boats, lines for the hours, and nothing left in either. Patience has a peg. Its line is wet wood.
Through the bakery glass a woman draws the blind. The loaves stay in the light. She did not look at you either.
He stands in his light and keeps his hands in the towel. "Board-keeper," he says before you ask. "Say what you want and go up."

charview.text: He stands in his light, hands in the towel.
charview.holding: He shuts the door on the book. The light goes with him.
charview.conversation: "Voss chalked his own hour. Clerks don't do that." He looks at the board. "He was letting the street read it."
"I washed it. A name on a board at night is a name said out loud." He steps back into the room. "Chalk washes off. A dry room does not."
"Don't stop on it. The sluice is harbor water with a lid on."
